description: Acceptance for the averaged and switched buck converters. The averaged reference is design/design.json (scipy, the same PID equations and limits, and the steady state at 15 V / 2 A). Three switched-model checks need switching to pass: the inductor-current peak at 2 + dI/2, the input-current peak, and the 20 kHz spectral line. The inductor-current valley and the ripple on every recorded row are one-sided bounds (continuous conduction, ripple not above the analytic value), and the means are time-weighted.

checks.note: design/design.json final_v: the 5 V reference after the 1 A load step and the 12 -> 15 V line step (run and design agree to 1e-9)
design/design.json pre_load_v, before the load step (run and design agree to 1e-8)
design/design.json mean_v_40_50: time-weighted mean after the line step
the 1 A load step at 20 ms dips the output to 4.82261 V (design load_min_v); the bound leaves 0.1 mV
the largest output, after the load-step recovery at 23.5 ms (design peak_v)
the startup inrush at 0.244 ms (design max_i); the 5 us output grid samples the sharp peak 3e-5 low
the load-step peak at 20.28 ms (design load_max_i)
1 A in the load resistor + 1 A load step at 5 V (design final_i)
steady duty (Vref + R_L*I)/Vin = (5 + 0.1*2)/15 (design final_duty)
the MTF conserves power: input current d*i_L = 0.3467*2 A (design final_iin)
input power 15 V * 0.6933 A = Pout 10 W + R_L*i^2 0.4 W (design mean_pin_40_50)
load power 5 V * 2 A (design mean_pout_40_50)
efficiency 10/10.4 = 96.15 %: the only loss is R_L (design final_efficiency)
no solver failure, causality conflict, derivative causality, algebraic loop or event-limit stop; W205 (the bond graph is Generic, so dimensionless) is expected
time-weighted mean of the switched output is the 5 V set point (measured 5.000006 V)
time-weighted mean inductor current is the 2 A load (measured 1.999996 A)
time-weighted load power 5 V * 2 A (measured 10.00002 W). Pin/y is a pulse train that jumps at every edge, so its row-based mean is biased; README gives its mean from the switch state
the inductor current peaks at 2 + dI/2 with dI = Vin*D*(1 - D)/(L*f_sw) = 0.361418 A at 15 V, D = 0.34667 (design steady_state_15V_2A); the averaged model stays at 2.000 A and fails this
the valley 2 - dI/2 = 1.819291 A (measured 1.819308 A); a lower bound only: it shows continuous conduction, the peak check above is what needs switching
the input current is the inductor current while the switch is on (MTF, modulus 1) and 0 while it is off, so it peaks at the inductor peak; the averaged input current is 0.693 A
the dominant line of the inductor current is the 20 kHz switching frequency
inductor ripple on every row (measured 0.36157 A pp) against dI = 0.361418 A pp at 15 V / 2 A (design); 1 % margin
output ripple on every row (measured 4.878 mV pp) against dV = dI/(8*f_sw*C) = 4.806 mV pp (no ESR, design)
the load-step dip with the switching ripple (measured 4.82567 V); the averaged design bottoms at 4.82261 V
the PWM edges are events; the run must not hit the event limit. W205 (Generic bond graph) is expected

compare.note: the switched output stays within half its ripple (dV/2 = 2.4 mV) of the averaged one; observed 2.63 mV
